evals.prompt: The accepted incident-triage workflow has one queue, a selected-incident detail drawer, and one primary action: Assign owner. The proposed visual brief adds a permanent activity column, a hero metric card, three nested bordered panels, and a bright animated background. Give the visual direction and implementation handoff.
evals.expected_output: Preserves the accepted workflow and makes the assignment action visually unmistakable; removes or defers nonessential visual layers; records a deliberate no; retains accessibility and necessary state visibility without a literal Steve Jobs imitation.
assertions: Names the user-facing benefit and keeps Assign owner as the visual focal action.
Removes or defers the permanent activity column, hero metric card, nested containers, or animated background unless evidence proves a primary-job need.
States a deliberate no instead of only saying the page should be minimal.
Preserves functional requirements, accessibility, and visible state treatment.
Returns visual-system constraints and an implementation handoff without reauthoring the interaction model.

farplane.title: Uses visual subtraction to protect a single operational focus

evals.prompt: New iPhone app for a neighborhood bakery's pre-order pickup. The workflow is settled: browse today's bakes, reserve, show a pickup code at the counter. There is no existing design system. Make it look good and not like every other ordering app.
evals.expected_output: Classifies the register, writes a scene sentence, names a concept from the bakery's world rather than an adjective, sketches three directions that differ in concept, picks one with reasons for rejecting the others, sets dials, and plans a key-screen render at phone viewport with critique before handoff.
assertions: Names a visual concept drawn from the bakery or neighborhood world, not only adjectives such as clean, warm, or premium.
Presents three directions that differ in concept, not only in palette, font, or radius.
Chooses one direction against the scene sentence, focal action, or dials and gives a reason each other direction lost.
Keeps the reserve action and pickup code clear; the concept does not hurt the primary job.

Renders a key screen as a static HTML mock at a phone viewport with realistic content and reports its path and critique scores, or labels the critique `unrendered` with the reason; a text-only critique without that label fails.
Avoids banned AI tells such as purple-blue gradients, identical icon card grids, and gradient text.

farplane.title: Starts a new direction from a domain concept and three compared directions

evals.prompt: Our accepted operator dashboard already has a dark token set and component library. The task list screen feels flat: every row has equal weight and the overdue items do not stand out. Polish it.
evals.expected_output: Treats this as polish of an existing design system: preserves tokens and components, does not invent a new concept or run three directions, fixes hierarchy with the smallest change, and re-renders and re-scores the screen.
assertions: Preserves the existing tokens and components instead of proposing a new visual system or palette.
Does not invent a new concept or run three new directions; names the existing concept or `none recorded`.
Fixes the hierarchy problem (overdue emphasis, row weight) with a small concrete change.
Reports a rendered screenshot path with scores after the fix, or labels the critique `unrendered` with the reason.

farplane.title: Polish of an accepted design system skips concept divergence

evals.prompt: New internal dispatch dashboard for a courier company: dispatchers watch about 40 live deliveries, spot late ones, and reassign drivers all shift long. No design system exists yet. Give the visual direction.
evals.expected_output: Treats this as product register for repeated work: names a concept from the courier world but keeps it quiet (accent, status color, icons, one signature moment) while layout stays dense and scannable; the three directions vary concept without turning the dashboard cinematic; dials stay in product or data-heavy ranges.
assertions: Classifies the surface as product or data-heavy register for repeated work.
Names a concept from the courier or dispatch world and limits it to accent, status color, icons, naming, or one signature moment rather than layout or decorative motion.
Keeps late deliveries and reassignment as the visual focus, scannable at about 40 rows.
Sets density at 6 or higher and motion at 4 or lower, or justifies any departure.
Does not propose a hero section, illustrated backgrounds, or cinematic motion for the working view.

farplane.title: Keeps a domain concept quiet on a repeated-use dashboard

evals.prompt: Redesign our landing page so it looks like a Vox explainer. Inspirations: Faction.ai (palette: black, white, #1E1E1E, stone #E8E1D9 and #DFD9CE, bronze #A48B69, muted #7A7368), TypeSafe.ai, and Design Arena. The functional basis is settled: one page, focal action 'Get my free AI plan'. A Vox tasty pack is available with an orange #F36B21 marker accent. Give the visual direction, render it, and get it ready to promote to the live page.
evals.expected_output: Builds a steal table per named reference with exact adopted values before any styling and asks the operator to approve it; keeps the Faction.ai palette and treats the tasty-pack orange as a conflict question rather than swapping it in; renders the mock, labels its own scores as a self-check, and gets the pass from a farplane:reviewer subagent or the operator with each steal-table trait checked side by side against a reference screenshot before promotion.
assertions: Writes a steal table before styling that maps each of Faction.ai, TypeSafe.ai, and Design Arena to adopted traits with exact values (hex, font, layout move), and asks the operator to approve it before building.
Uses the operator's Faction.ai palette values; does not introduce orange #F36B21 or another tasty-pack accent as a role color without first asking the operator about the conflict.
Labels any score the author gives its own render as a self-check and does not report `pass` from it.
Routes the promotion verdict to a farplane:reviewer subagent or the operator, with the screenshot, steal table, and reference screenshots as inputs.
The critique includes a per-trait reference check with each trait marked visible, missing, or changed beside its reference screenshot; a missing or changed trait blocks promotion.
Does not promote the mock to the live page before the independent pass.

farplane.title: Keeps operator references and palette, and gets an independent pass before promotion
